altitude.note: Altitude of the Tunka-133 array; the other TAIGA instruments are in the same valley and their altitudes are not separately stated.
altitude.quote: The Tunka-133 array is located at an altitude of 670 m a.s.l.

coordinates.note: A valley-scale position from the TAIGA collaboration's overview paper (0.01 degree, about 1 km); the arrays extend over about 3 km2 and no survey position of any detector is given in the sources read.
coordinates.quote: in the Tunka valley 50 km to the west from Lake Baikal (51.49 N, 103.04 E)

place.region: Tunka valley, Eastern Siberia (near the southern tip of Lake Baikal)

summary.plain: A broad valley in Siberia, 50 km west of the southern tip of Lake Baikal, where Russian and international teams have run cosmic-ray and gamma-ray detectors since 1993.
summary.technical: Tunka valley (51.49 N, 103.04 E, about 670 m): site of the Tunka-4/-25/-133 Cherenkov arrays, Tunka-Rex, Tunka-Grande and the TAIGA-HiSCORE and TAIGA-IACT detectors.
